flags: Cache 00 gives the byway as 414 miles; cache 01 gives Minnesota US 75 as 408 miles. Their measurement scopes are not explained, so total mileage is omitted.

Cache 30 uses Yankton Dakota and Yankton people; cache 39 uses Yankton Sioux Tribe of Indians and several historical legal variants. The court account uses the case-title name. No tribal-authored page is supplied to resolve present preferred terminology.

The current story’s universal neutral-ground claim is omitted: cache 30 states it broadly and cache 39 recounts gathering under truce, but neither establishes unrestricted access for every nation across all periods.
Cache 39 establishes ownership and entitlement to compensation and reverses the dismissal; it does not establish subsequent payment or return of the land. Neither outcome is claimed.

The Noyes closure, surviving building and practical diversion are supported by cached Wikipedia pages only; no current border-agency page is supplied. The checked date records cache saving, not live verification.
The auto-trail history does not establish that every part of the modern byway follows the original alignment; no exact alignment continuity is claimed.
The Pipestone notice uses the cached Wikipedia trail description; no current land-manager trail-status page is supplied.

Driving description is thinner than Cherohala’s: the cache supports prairie, farmland, Lake Benton’s Buffalo Ridge setting and the flat former lakebed around Moorhead, but does not establish long straight stretches, Minnesota lane counts or a whole-route driving time. The lake, wind-farm and town pages do not establish lake or turbine sightlines from US 75. These views and driving characteristics are not claimed. The overview stays shorter rather than supplying them.

Explore Minnesota identifies the scenic byway and describes its scenery and attractions; the cache does not supply a route-specific designation finding or designation date. No formal scenic-selection rationale or National Scenic Byway status is claimed.
